questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. Sachchidananda Sinha was the provisional President of the Assembly when it first met in December 1946.
2. The Objectives Resolution was adopted by the Assembly on 22 January 1947.
3. The Drafting Committee was chaired by B. N. Rau.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Drafting Committee was chaired by B. R. Ambedkar; B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser who prepared the initial draft. Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted about six weeks later.

questions.q:
Match the following cases with the subject they dealt with:
Case
A. K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
B. Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
C. Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
D. NALSA v. Union of India
Subject
1. Right to privacy as a fundamental right
2. Striking down of Section 66A of the Information Technology Act
3. Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace
4. Legal recognition of transgender persons as a third gender
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: Puttaswamy (2017) located privacy within Article 21. Shreya Singhal (2015) struck Section 66A as vague and chilling to speech, Vishaka (1997) laid down guidelines under Articles 14, 15 and 21 until legislation, and NALSA (2014) recognised a third gender.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 7 and Ch 9; Supreme Court judgments

questions.q:
Which of the following Directive Principles are based on Gandhian ideology?
1. Article 40: Organisation of village panchayats
2. Article 44: Uniform civil code
3. Article 43: Promotion of cottage industries
4. Article 47: Prohibition of intoxicating drinks
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Village panchayats, cottage industries and prohibition are classified as Gandhian principles. The uniform civil code is a liberal-intellectual principle.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He must be a person qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. He has the right to vote in the Houses of Parliament.
3. He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 88 the Attorney General may speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House and its committees but cannot vote. The office has no fixed tenure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Parliamentary Committees:
1. The Public Accounts Committee consists of 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Estimates Committee includes members of both Houses of Parliament.
3. The Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed from the ruling party.
4. The Comptroller and Auditor General assists the Public Accounts Committee.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, and by convention since 1967 the PAC chair goes to the Opposition. The CAG's audit reports are the basis of the PAC's work.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it?
questions.e: Article 142 is the Supreme Court's special power to do complete justice. Article 136 gives special leave to appeal and Article 141 makes the law declared by the Court binding on all courts.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 249:
1. Parliament can legislate on a State List subject if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. The resolution must be passed by both Houses of Parliament.
3. A law so made ceases to have effect six months after the resolution ceases to be in force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only the Rajya Sabha, as the representative of the States, must pass the resolution declaring it necessary in the national interest. The resolution lasts one year at a time and may be renewed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indra Sawhney case (1992):
1. The Supreme Court upheld the 27 percent reservation for Other Backward Classes in Central Government jobs.
2. The Court held that reservation should not, as a rule, exceed 50 percent.
3. The Court held that reservation in promotions is permissible.
4. The Court applied the creamy layer exclusion to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Indra Sawhney held that Article 16(4) does not extend to promotions and that the creamy layer exclusion applies to OBCs, not SC/ST. Reservation in promotions was later enabled by the 77th Amendment.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned before any court.
Statement-II: Article 329 bars the courts from questioning the validity of laws relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 329(a) bars judicial interference in delimitation and seat allotment, and the Delimitation Act gives the Commission's orders the force of law. The bar exists so that elections are not stalled by litigation over boundaries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. A Public Information Officer must generally provide the information within 30 days of the request.
2. A second appeal against the decision of the first appellate authority lies directly to the High Court.
3. Information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be provided within 48 hours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The second appeal lies to the Central or State Information Commission, not the High Court. The 48-hour window for life and liberty matters is a special fast track.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Satara was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse during Dalhousie's tenure.
2. Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance.
3. The Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed during Dalhousie's tenure as Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dalhousie left India in February 1856 and the Widow Remarriage Act was passed in July 1856 under Canning. Awadh was taken over on grounds of misrule rather than through the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Revolt of 1857:
1. The General Service Enlistment Act, 1856 required new sepoys to be ready to serve overseas.
2. Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore in March 1857.
3. The Revolt began at Kanpur on 4 June 1857.
4. Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed Emperor of Hindustan at Lucknow.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, and Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed Emperor at Delhi the next day. Overseas service would have meant loss of caste for high-caste sepoys.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Theosophical Society headquarters in India : Adyar
questions.e: The Ahmadiyya Movement was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889. Syed Ahmad Khan led the Aligarh Movement and founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Formation of the Swaraj Party
2. Chauri Chaura incident
3. Special Calcutta session of the Congress approving the Non-Cooperation Movement
4. Bardoli resolution suspending the Non-Cooperation Movement
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Calcutta session was in September 1920, Chauri Chaura on 5 February 1922 and the Bardoli resolution a week later. The disillusioned leaders C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru then formed the Swaraj Party in January 1923.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It introduced diarchy in the provinces.
2. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
3. It separated Sind from Bombay and Orissa from Bihar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act abolished diarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy, while diarchy was proposed at the Centre. The proposed All-India Federation never came into being.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the 1937 elections, the Congress won a majority in five of the eleven provinces.
2. The Congress ministries resigned in 1942 following the Quit India Movement.
3. The Muslim League observed a 'Day of Deliverance' in December 1939 after the Congress ministries resigned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 to protest India being dragged into the war without consultation. Jinnah then called for a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Statement-I: Ashoka appointed Dhamma Mahamatras in the thirteenth year of his reign.
Statement-II: Their task was to propagate Dhamma and look after the welfare of people of all sects.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The Mahamatras were a special cadre created to carry the policy of Dhamma to the people, including different religious communities. They show how Ashoka turned the post-Kalinga moral change into administration.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History I, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of inscription and ruler is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: The Aihole inscription was composed by Ravikirti for the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, who defeated Harsha. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jainism:
1. Parshvanatha prescribed four vows, to which Mahavira added the vow of celibacy.
2. The split into Digambara and Svetambara sects is traditionally linked with Bhadrabahu's migration to the south during a famine.
3. The first Jain council was held at Vallabhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first council was held at Pataliputra under Sthulabhadra, while the second at Vallabhi in the early sixth century CE finalised the Agamas. Digambaras remained naked and Svetambaras wore white.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Themes in Indian History; Spectrum

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bahmani Sultanate was founded by Mahmud Gawan.
2. Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara wrote the Telugu work Amuktamalyada.
3. Mahmud Gawan, a minister of the Bahmani Sultan, built a madrasa at Bidar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah with its capital at Gulbarga. Mahmud Gawan was the chief minister who reorganised the kingdom in the 15th century.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of folk painting and State is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Phad is a scroll painting tradition of Rajasthan, narrating the epics of local deities such as Pabuji. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture, Ch 'Painting'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Presidents of the Indian National Congress:
1. Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President, at the 1887 Madras session.
2. Annie Besant was the first woman President, at the 1917 Lucknow session.
3. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President, at the 1925 Kanpur session.
4. George Yule was the first English President, in 1888.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Annie Besant presided over the 1917 Calcutta session, not Lucknow. The Lucknow session of 1916 was presided over by A. C. Majumdar.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Which of the following are depositional landforms?
1. Delta
2. Alluvial fan
3. Yardang
4. Barchan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: A yardang is an erosional ridge carved by wind abrasion. Deltas and alluvial fans are fluvial deposits and barchans are crescent-shaped dunes built by deposition of sand.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 6 and 7

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On 21 June, the Sun's rays fall vertically over the Tropic of Cancer.
2. The Earth is at aphelion around 4 July.
3. The Northern Hemisphere has its longest day on 22 December.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: On 22 December the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn and the Northern Hemisphere has its shortest day. Seasons are caused by the axial tilt, not the Earth-Sun distance, as the Earth is farthest in the northern summer.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 3

questions.q:
Statement-I: Spring tides have the largest tidal range and occur on full moon and new moon days.
Statement-II: On those days the Sun, Moon and Earth lie in a straight line, so the gravitational pulls of the Sun and Moon reinforce each other.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Alignment adds the solar pull to the lunar pull and raises high tides and lowers low tides. At the quarter moons the pulls act at right angles and produce neap tides.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 13

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of temperate grassland and country is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: The Llanos are the tropical savanna grasslands of Venezuela and Colombia, the Orinoco basin. Brazil's savanna is the Campos.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography / Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about pre-monsoon weather in India:
1. 'Mango showers' in Kerala and Karnataka help the ripening of mangoes.
2. Kalbaisakhi are thunderstorms that occur in West Bengal in the pre-monsoon season.
3. 'Loo' refers to cold winds blowing from the Himalayas in winter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Loo is a hot, dry wind blowing over the northern plains in May and June. Mango showers and Kalbaisakhi are convective pre-monsoon rain events.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of laterite soil?
o: It is rich in humus and nitrogen
It is formed by intense leaching under heavy rainfall
It is rich in iron and aluminium oxides
It can support crops such as cashew with the use of manures
questions.e: Heavy rain leaches away silica, nitrogen and humus, and high temperature destroys organic matter, so laterite is poor in them. Manuring is needed for crops.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 6

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
questions.e: The five Caspian littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan. Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked.
questions.s: Atlas / NCERT Class XI World Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Gini coefficient of one indicates perfect equality of income distribution.
2. The farther the Lorenz curve is from the line of equality, the greater the inequality.
3. The Lorenz curve lies above the line of equality.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A Gini of zero means perfect equality and one means perfect inequality. The Lorenz curve sags below the line of equality because the poorest groups hold a smaller share of income than of population.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'Growth and Development'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Disinflation means a fall in the general price level.
2. Core inflation excludes food and fuel prices.
3. Stagflation is a situation of high inflation along with high unemployment and low growth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Disinflation is a slowing of the inflation rate and prices still rise; a fall in the general price level is deflation. Core inflation strips out volatile food and fuel items to show the underlying trend.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of an economy is Rs 330 lakh crore and the GDP deflator is 110. The real GDP (in base-year prices) is:
questions.e: Real GDP is nominal GDP divided by the deflator and multiplied by 100, so 330 divided by 110 times 100 gives 300. A deflator above 100 means prices have risen since the base year, so real GDP is less than nominal.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'National Income'

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court
Salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General
Salaries and allowances of Union Ministers
questions.e: Charged expenditure is not subject to a vote in Parliament, though it can be discussed. Ministers' salaries are voted as part of the demands for grants.

questions.q: The equity of Regional Rural Banks is held by:
o: Central Government 50 percent, State Government 25 percent and sponsor bank 25 percent
Central Government 35 percent, State Government 15 percent and sponsor bank 50 percent
Central Government 51 percent, State Government 24 percent and sponsor bank 25 percent
Central Government 50 percent, State Government 15 percent and sponsor bank 35 percent
questions.e: The Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976 fixed the ownership as 50:15:35 among the Centre, the State and the sponsor commercial bank. RRBs were set up following the Narasimham Working Group.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sensex is a stock market index of 30 companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
2. The Nifty 50 is computed on the basis of simple price weighting.
3. The Sensex is calculated on the free-float market capitalisation method.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both the Sensex and the Nifty 50 use free-float market capitalisation weighting, not simple price weighting. Larger companies therefore move the index more.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'Financial Markets'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about e-NAM:
1. It is a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing agricultural produce mandis.
2. It was launched in 2016.
3. It is implemented by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: e-NAM is implemented by the Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) under the Ministry of Agriculture. It integrates APMC mandis into a unified national market.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999:
1. It replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973.
2. A contravention of FEMA is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment.
3. Its objective is to prohibit all foreign exchange transactions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: FEMA is a civil law whose objective is to facilitate external trade and payments and promote an orderly foreign exchange market. FERA was a stringent regime with criminal penalties.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Ch 'External Sector'

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of ecological interaction and example is NOT correctly matched?
o: Parasitism : Rhizobium in the root nodules of legumes
Commensalism : An orchid growing on a mango tree
questions.e: Rhizobium and the legume exchange nitrogen and sugars, so this is mutualism. The orchid only gains support from the tree without harming it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the nitrogen cycle:
1. Nitrosomonas converts ammonia into nitrite.
2. Nitrobacter reduces nitrate to molecular nitrogen.
3. Anabaena, a cyanobacterium, can fix atmospheric nitrogen.
4. The nitrogen cycle has no major atmospheric reservoir.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nitrobacter oxidises nitrite to nitrate; the return of N2 to air is done by denitrifiers such as Pseudomonas. Nitrogen has a huge atmospheric reservoir (about 78 percent of air), unlike the phosphorus cycle.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Ecology chapter; NCERT Class XII Biology

questions.q:
Arrange the following IUCN Red List categories in decreasing order of extinction risk:
1. Vulnerable
2. Critically Endangered
3. Near Threatened
4. Endangered
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The threatened categories run Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, and Near Threatened sits just below them. Extinct and Extinct in the Wild are above all of them.

questions.q: The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by:
o: The Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: The NBWL is the apex advisory body for wildlife conservation and is chaired by the Prime Minister; its Standing Committee is chaired by the Environment Minister. It was given statutory status by the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of convention and the city hosting its secretariat is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn, Germany. The Ramsar secretariat is at Gland, Switzerland, and CITES is at Geneva.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Green Climate Fund is headquartered in Songdo, South Korea.
2. COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh agreed to establish a fund for loss and damage.
3. The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP26 in Glasgow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 in 2015. COP26 at Glasgow produced the Glasgow Climate Pact in 2021.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of disease and causative pollutant is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Itai-itai disease in Japan was caused by cadmium contamination of rice and water. Lead causes plumbism.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian launch vehicles:
1. The PSLV has a cryogenic upper stage.
2. LVM3 was used to launch Chandrayaan-3.
3. The SSLV is designed to launch small satellites into low Earth orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PSLV uses solid and liquid (Vikas) stages with no cryogenic stage, which is why GTO missions of heavy satellites need the GSLV or LVM3 with the cryogenic CE-20 stage.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the James Webb Space Telescope:
1. It observes primarily in the ultraviolet part of the spectrum.
2. It orbits the Earth in low Earth orbit like the Hubble Space Telescope.
3. Its primary mirror is made of 18 hexagonal segments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The JWST is an infrared telescope stationed near the Sun-Earth L2 point, about 1.5 million km away, so its sunshield can keep the instruments cold. Hubble orbits the Earth.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors, heavy water is used as a moderator.
2. Control rods in a nuclear reactor slow down fast neutrons.
3. ITER, an international nuclear fusion project, is being built in France and India is one of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Control rods, made of boron or cadmium, absorb neutrons to regulate the chain reaction; it is the moderator that slows neutrons. ITER at Cadarache is a tokamak that aims to demonstrate fusion power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Silicon doped with phosphorus becomes an n-type semiconductor.
2. Laser light is produced by stimulated emission of radiation.
3. A light-emitting diode works on the principle of the photoelectric effect.
4. Optical fibre communication works on the principle of total internal reflection.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: An LED emits light by electroluminescence when electrons and holes recombine at the p-n junction, whereas the photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons by light. Phosphorus has five valence electrons and adds free electrons to silicon.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. INS Vikrant, commissioned in 2022, was built at the Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders.
2. INS Vikramaditya was acquired from Russia.
3. INS Arihant is India's first indigenous nuclear-powered attack submarine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: INS Vikrant was built at Cochin Shipyard Limited, and INS Arihant is a nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), not an attack submarine. INS Vikramaditya is the refitted Admiral Gorshkov.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
2. Fullerenes are cage-like molecules of carbon, such as C60.
3. Carbon nanotubes have very high tensile strength.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. They are all allotropes of carbon with nanoscale structures: sheet (graphene), ball (fullerene) and tube (nanotube).
questions.s: NCERT Class XI and XII Chemistry
